content.text: : USU an ascending infect of the lower urinary tract from the urethra
▪︎lower abd pain; may note gross hematuria; suprapubic tenderness w/o rebound or mass
, hematuria, WBCs esterase, nitrites, cloudy urine, bacteriuria
▪︎flank tenderness, N/V, or fever → eval + tx for pyelo (urine cx + IV abx)
▪︎≥100,000 CFU/mL (10⁵) of a single organism → UTI
▪︎TMP-SMX BID x3d or nitrofurantoin 100mg BID x5d
▪︎other 1st-line: fosfomycin 3g x1; pivmecillinam 400mg BID x3–7d (cost/availability limit)
▪︎FQs (ex, cipro): effective but reserve for pts w/o alternatives (⇡serious SEs, ex, tendon rupture)
▪︎amoxicillin: poor efficacy vs E. coli, S. saprophyticus, Proteus, Klebsiella
▪︎preg: tx asymptomatic bacteriuria (⇡risk of preterm birth, LBW, perinatal mortality)
Infect of the upper GU tract (kidney parenchyma & renal pelvis)
: USU an ascending infect of the lower urinary tract
▪︎gram (−) bact MC: E. coli, Pseudomonas, Enterobacter, Proteus, Klebsiella; also enterococci, S. aureus, S. saprophyticus
▪︎Proteus mirabilis (+ other urease-producing bact) → struvite stones
: DM, hx of recurr UTIs or kidney stones, preg, congenital urinary tract malformations
▪︎more common in young adult ♀; RF also recent frequent intercourse, UTI in past yr, new sex partner, recent spermicide use
▪︎eval: UA, CBC, urine cx (heavy growth; sensitivities guide abx) + blood cx
▪︎imaging ⍉needed initially; ⍉response w/in 48h, severely ill, or sus comps/obstruct → CT abd/pelvis w/ + w/o contrast (study of choice): focal ⇣perfusion or perinephric fat stranding (nonspecific)
▪︎US if can't tolerate contrast/radiation → hydronephrosis from a stone or other obstruct
▪︎cipro or levofloxacin x5–7d; ⍉FQ → ceftriaxone 1g IM/IV x1, then PO TMP-SMX, Augmentin, cefpodoxime, cefdinir, or cefadroxil x10–14d
▪︎mild-mod: IV ceftriaxone, cipro, levofloxacin, or aztreonam; severe: IV cefepime, pip-tazo, or meropenem
▪︎critical illness, obstruct, or MDR risk: antipseudomonal carbapenem (imipenem, meropenem, doripenem) + vanco (consider MRSA, VRE, ESBL coverage); ⍉MDR RFs → ceftriaxone or pip-tazo
▪︎IV until afebrile x24h → PO abx x14d
: older age, signs of obstruct, comorbid conditions, inability to tolerate PO abx
▪︎also admit: significant fever, tachy, dehydration, sepsis, sig ⇣kidney funct, ⍉PO, or ⍉response to outpt abx w/in 48h
▪︎fevers may persist up to 72h after abx; most recover full kidney funct
▪︎comps: kidney + perinephric abscess, papillary necrosis, emphysematous pyelo (rare, necrotizing, gas-forming; assoc w/ DM), pyonephrosis, sepsis, shock, AKI
